title: openDesk federates the sovereign desktop but holds no auditable record of the administrative decisions taken in it
content:
openDesk is ZenDiS's sovereign workplace suite for German public administration. It federates the desktop: separate tools are assembled into one workplace that an administration can run under its own control. That federation is the achievement, and it concerns where software runs and who governs it.

What it does not provide is a record of the administrative decisions taken inside it. Work is spread across the suite's components, each holding its own state, and nothing sits underneath them asserting that a decision was made, by which official, under which rule. Sovereignty over tooling and auditability of the acts performed with that tooling are separate properties, and only the first has been delivered.

For B1 Systems, which delivers openDesk, the gap lands inside a requirement its customers already carry. Public-sector audit asks precisely for the attributed decision record, so the argument is not a new capability that has to be explained from first principles but an existing obligation the current stack answers only in part.
